questions.text: Let $[x]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. Then the domain of $f(x)=\sec^{-1}(2[x]+1)$ is :
questions.sol:
$\sec^{-1}t$ needs $|t|\ge1$. With $t=2[x]+1$ (an odd integer), $|2[x]+1|\ge1$ always holds, since an odd integer is never 0.
Check: $[x]\ge0$ gives $t\ge1$; $[x]\le-1$ gives $t\le-1$.
So the domain is $(-\infty,\infty)$.

questions.text: Let $f:[0, 3]\to A$ be defined by $f(x)=2x^3-15x^2+36x+7$ and $g:[0, \infty)\to B$ be defined by $g(x)=\dfrac{x^{2025}}{x^{2025}+1}$. If both the functions are onto and $S=\{x\in\mathbf{Z}: x\in A \text{ or } x\in B\}$, then $n(S)$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}-\{0\}\to(-\infty, 1)$ be a polynomial of degree 2, satisfying $f(x)f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)=f(x)+f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$. If $f(K)=-2K$, then the sum of squares of all possible values of K is :
questions.sol:
A polynomial with $f(x)f(1/x)=f(x)+f(1/x)$ has the form $f(x)=1\pm x^n$; degree 2 gives $1\pm x^2$.
The values must be less than 1, so $f(x)=1-x^2$.
$1-K^2=-2K \Rightarrow K^2-2K-1=0$, roots with sum 2 and product $-1$.
Sum of squares $=2^2-2(-1)=6$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\alpha+i\beta$ and $\gamma+i\delta$ are the roots of $x^2-(3-2i)x-(2i-2)=0$, $i=\sqrt{-1}$, then $\alpha\gamma+\beta\delta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Discriminant $=(3-2i)^2+4(2i-2)=5-12i+8i-8=-3-4i=(1-2i)^2$.
Roots $=\dfrac{(3-2i)\pm(1-2i)}{2}=2-2i,\ 1$.
So $\alpha=2,\beta=-2,\gamma=1,\delta=0$ (either order gives the same value): $\alpha\gamma+\beta\delta=2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}&-2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $P=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$, $\theta>0$. If $B=PAP^T$, $C=P^TB^{10}P$ and the sum of the diagonal elements of C is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, where $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $m+n$ is :
questions.sol:
$P$ is orthogonal ($P^TP=I$), so $B^{10}=PA^{10}P^T$ and $C=P^TB^{10}P=A^{10}$.
$A$ is upper triangular, so $A^{10}$ has diagonal $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)^{10}=\dfrac1{32}$ and $1$.
Trace $=\dfrac{33}{32}$, so $m+n=65$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: For positive integers n, if $4a_n=(n^2+5n+6)$ and $S_n=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{a_k}\right)$, then the value of $507\,S_{2025}$ is :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac1{a_k}=\dfrac{4}{(k+2)(k+3)}=4\left(\dfrac1{k+2}-\dfrac1{k+3}\right)$, which telescopes.
$S_n=4\left(\dfrac13-\dfrac1{n+3}\right)$, so $S_{2025}=4\left(\dfrac13-\dfrac1{2028}\right)=\dfrac{4\times675}{2028}$.
$507\,S_{2025}=\dfrac{2700}{4}=675$.

questions.text: Let the coefficients of three consecutive terms $T_r$, $T_{r+1}$ and $T_{r+2}$ in the binomial expansion of $(a+b)^{12}$ be in a G.P. and let p be the number of all possible values of r. Let q be the sum of all rational terms in the binomial expansion of $\left(\sqrt[4]{3}+\sqrt[3]{4}\right)^{12}$. Then $p+q$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The coefficients are $\binom{12}{r-1},\binom{12}{r},\binom{12}{r+1}$. G.P. needs equal ratios: $\dfrac{13-r}{r}=\dfrac{12-r}{r+1}$, i.e. $(13-r)(r+1)=r(12-r)$, which reduces to $13=0$. So $p=0$.
General term $\binom{12}{k}3^{(12-k)/4}4^{k/3}$ is rational when $4\mid(12-k)$ and $3\mid k$: $k=0$ or $12$.
$q=3^3+4^4=27+256=283$, so $p+q=283$.

questions.text: Let S be the set of all the words that can be formed by arranging all the letters of the word GARDEN. From the set S, one word is selected at random. The probability that the selected word will NOT have vowels in alphabetical order is :
questions.sol:
The vowels are A and E. In any arrangement A comes before E or after E, and by symmetry each happens in exactly half of the $6!$ words.
So the probability that they are not in alphabetical order is $\dfrac12$.

questions.text: Bag $B_1$ contains 6 white and 4 blue balls, Bag $B_2$ contains 4 white and 6 blue balls, and Bag $B_3$ contains 5 white and 5 blue balls. One of the bags is selected at random and a ball is drawn from it. If the ball is white, then the probability, that the ball is drawn from Bag $B_2$, is :
questions.sol:
$P(W)=\dfrac13\left(\dfrac{6}{10}+\dfrac{4}{10}+\dfrac{5}{10}\right)=\dfrac12$.
By Bayes' theorem, $P(B_2\mid W)=\dfrac{\frac13\cdot\frac{4}{10}}{\frac12}=\dfrac{4}{15}$.

questions.text: Two equal sides of an isosceles triangle are along $-x+2y=4$ and $x+y=4$. If m is the slope of its third side, then the sum, of all possible distinct values of m, is :
questions.sol:
The equal sides have slopes $\dfrac12$ and $-1$; the third side makes equal angles with both.
$\left|\dfrac{m-\frac12}{1+\frac m2}\right|=\left|\dfrac{m+1}{1-m}\right|$, i.e. $\dfrac{2m-1}{2+m}=\pm\dfrac{m+1}{1-m}$.
With $+$: $3m^2+3=0$, no real root. With $-$: $m^2-6m-1=0$, two real roots with sum $6$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the midpoint of a chord of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1$ is $\left(\sqrt{2}, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$, and the length of the chord is $\dfrac{2\sqrt{\alpha}}{3}$, then $\alpha$ is :
questions.sol:
Chord with given midpoint: $T=S_1$, i.e. $\dfrac{\sqrt2x}{9}+\dfrac{4y}{12}=\dfrac29+\dfrac49$, which simplifies to $\sqrt2x+3y=6$.
Substituting $y=\dfrac{6-\sqrt2x}{3}$: $4x^2+(6-\sqrt2x)^2=36 \Rightarrow 6x^2-12\sqrt2x=0$, so $x=0$ or $2\sqrt2$.
End points $(0,2)$ and $\left(2\sqrt2,\dfrac23\right)$; length$^2=8+\dfrac{16}{9}=\dfrac{88}{9}$, length $=\dfrac{2\sqrt{22}}{3}$.
$\alpha=22$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If A and B are the points of intersection of the circle $x^2+y^2-8x=0$ and the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{9}-\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1$ and a point P moves on the line $2x-3y+4=0$, then the centroid of $\Delta PAB$ lies on the line :
questions.sol:
From the hyperbola, $y^2=\dfrac{4x^2}{9}-4$. Then $x^2+\dfrac{4x^2}{9}-4-8x=0 \Rightarrow 13x^2-72x-36=0 \Rightarrow x=6$ or $-\dfrac{6}{13}$.
$x=-\dfrac6{13}$ gives $y^2<0$, so $A,B=(6,\pm2\sqrt3)$.
Centroid $(h,k)$: $P=(3h-12,\,3k)$. On the line: $2(3h-12)-9k+4=0$, i.e. $6x-9y=20$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{13}\left\{\frac{1}{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+(r-1)\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{r\pi}{6}\right)}\right\}=a\sqrt{3}+b$, $a, b\in\mathbf{Z}$, then $a^2+b^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
With $\theta_r=\dfrac\pi4+(r-1)\dfrac\pi6$, the angles differ by $\dfrac\pi6$, and $\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta_r\sin\theta_{r+1}}=\dfrac{\cot\theta_r-\cot\theta_{r+1}}{\sin\frac\pi6}=2(\cot\theta_r-\cot\theta_{r+1})$.
Sum $=2\left(\cot\dfrac\pi4-\cot\left(\dfrac\pi4+\dfrac{13\pi}{6}\right)\right)=2\left(1-\cot\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\right)=2(1-(2-\sqrt3))=2\sqrt3-2$.
$a=2$, $b=-2$, $a^2+b^2=8$.

questions.text: Let A, B, C be three points in $xy$-plane, whose position vector are given by $\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}$, $\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}$ and $a\hat{i}+(1-a)\hat{j}$ respectively with respect to the origin O. If the distance of the point C from the line bisecting the angle between the vectors $\overrightarrow{OA}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}$ is $\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{2}}$, then the sum of all the possible values of a is :
questions.sol:
$|\overrightarrow{OA}|=|\overrightarrow{OB}|=2$, so the bisector is along $\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{OB}=(1+\sqrt3)(\hat i+\hat j)$: the line $y=x$.
Distance of $C(a,1-a)$ from $x-y=0$: $\dfrac{|2a-1|}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt2} \Rightarrow a=5$ or $-4$.
Sum $=1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the components of $\vec{a}=\alpha\hat{i}+\beta\hat{j}+\gamma\hat{k}$ along and perpendicular to $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ respectively, are $\dfrac{16}{11}\left(3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)$ and $\dfrac{1}{11}\left(-4\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-17\hat{k}\right)$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\vec a$ is the sum of its two components: $\dfrac{1}{11}\left[(48-4)\hat i+(16-5)\hat j+(-16-17)\hat k\right]=4\hat i+\hat j-3\hat k$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=16+1+9=26$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The square of the distance of the point $\left(\dfrac{15}{7}, \dfrac{32}{7}, 7\right)$ from the line $\dfrac{x+1}{3}=\dfrac{y+3}{5}=\dfrac{z+5}{7}$ in the direction of the vector $\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+7\hat{k}$ is :
questions.sol:
Move from the point along $(1,4,7)$: $\left(\dfrac{15}{7}+t,\ \dfrac{32}{7}+4t,\ 7+7t\right)$. A point of the line is $(-1+3s,\ -3+5s,\ -5+7s)$.
$z$: $s=t+\dfrac{12}{7}$. $x$: $\dfrac{15}{7}+t=-1+3t+\dfrac{36}{7} \Rightarrow t=-1$ (and $y$ checks: both give $\dfrac47$).
Distance$^2=t^2(1+16+49)=66$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(2)=1$. If $F(x)=xf(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbf{R}$, $\displaystyle\int_0^2 xF'(x)\,dx=6$ and $\displaystyle\int_0^2 x^2F''(x)\,dx=40$, then $F'(2)+\displaystyle\int_0^2 F(x)\,dx$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$F(2)=2f(2)=2$.
By parts: $\displaystyle\int_0^2xF'\,dx=[xF]_0^2-\int_0^2F\,dx=4-\int_0^2F\,dx=6$, so $\displaystyle\int_0^2F\,dx=-2$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^2x^2F''\,dx=[x^2F']_0^2-2\int_0^2xF'\,dx=4F'(2)-12=40$, so $F'(2)=13$.
Required value $=13-2=11$.

questions.text: Let $f$ be a real valued continuous function defined on the positive real axis such that $g(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x t\,f(t)\,dt$. If $g(x^3)=x^6+x^7$, then value of $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{15}f(r^3)$ is :
questions.sol:
Differentiate $g(x^3)=x^6+x^7$: $3x^2\cdot x^3f(x^3)=6x^5+7x^6$, so $f(x^3)=2+\dfrac{7x}{3}$.
$\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{15}f(r^3)=30+\frac73\cdot120=30+280=310$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $f(x)=\displaystyle\int\frac{1}{x^{1/4}\left(1+x^{1/4}\right)}dx$, $f(0)=-6$, then $f(1)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Put $x=t^4$, $dx=4t^3dt$: $\displaystyle\int\frac{4t^3}{t(1+t)}dt=4\int\left(t-1+\frac1{1+t}\right)dt=4\left(\frac{t^2}{2}-t+\ln(1+t)\right)+c$.
$f(0)=c=-6$.
$f(1)=4\left(\dfrac12-1+\ln2\right)-6=4\ln2-8=4(\log_e2-2)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the curves $x(1+y^2)=1$ and $y^2=2x$ is:
questions.sol:
Intersection: $\dfrac{y^2}{2}=\dfrac{1}{1+y^2} \Rightarrow y^4+y^2-2=0 \Rightarrow y=\pm1$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\left(\frac1{1+y^2}-\frac{y^2}{2}\right)dy=2\left(\frac\pi4-\frac16\right)=\frac\pi2-\frac13$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The interior angles of a polygon with n sides, are in an A.P. with common difference $6^\circ$. If the largest interior angle of the polygon is $219^\circ$, then n is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Angles $219^\circ, 213^\circ, \ldots$; their sum is $\dfrac n2\left[2(219)-6(n-1)\right]=n(222-3n)$.
This equals $(n-2)180$: $3n^2-42n-360=0 \Rightarrow n^2-14n-120=0 \Rightarrow n=20$ (rejecting $-6$).
Check: the smallest angle is $219-114=105^\circ$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The number of natural numbers, between 212 and 999, such that the sum of their digits is 15, is __________.
questions.sol:
Three-digit numbers $\overline{abc}$ with $a+b+c=15$: for each $a$, count pairs $(b,c)$ of digits with $b+c=15-a$.
$a=1,\ldots,9$ give $5,6,7,8,9,10,9,8,7$: total $69$.
Those not above 212: all 5 with $a=1$; with $a=2$ we need $b+c=13$, so $b\ge4$ and the number exceeds 212.
Answer $=69-5=64$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let A and B be the two points of intersection of the line $y+5=0$ and the mirror image of the parabola $y^2=4x$ with respect to the line $x+y+4=0$. If d denotes the distance between A and B, and a denotes the area of $\Delta SAB$, where S is the focus of the parabola $y^2=4x$, then the value of $(a+d)$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Reflection in $x+y+4=0$ sends $(x,y)$ to $(-y-4,\,-x-4)$. So $(x,y)$ is on the image when $(-y-4,-x-4)$ is on $y^2=4x$: $(x+4)^2=-4(y+4)$.
With $y=-5$: $(x+4)^2=4$, so $A(-2,-5)$, $B(-6,-5)$ and $d=4$.
$S=(1,0)$ is at height 5 above $AB$: $a=\dfrac12\cdot4\cdot5=10$.
$a+d=14$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{r=0}^{n}\left(\frac{\tan\left(x/2^{r+1}\right)+\tan^3\left(x/2^{r+1}\right)}{1-\tan^2\left(x/2^{r+1}\right)}\right)$. Then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^x-e^{f(x)}}{(x-f(x))}$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
With $t=\tan\theta$: $\tan2\theta-\tan\theta=t\left(\dfrac{2}{1-t^2}-1\right)=\dfrac{t(1+t^2)}{1-t^2}$, which is the given term for $\theta=x/2^{r+1}$.
So the sum telescopes: $\tan x-\tan\left(x/2^{n+1}\right)\to\tan x$, i.e. $f(x)=\tan x$.
$\dfrac{e^x-e^{\tan x}}{x-\tan x}=e^{\tan x}\cdot\dfrac{e^{x-\tan x}-1}{x-\tan x}\to1\cdot1=1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $y=y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation, $\sqrt{4-x^2}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\left(\left(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right)^2-y\right)\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$, $-2\le x\le2$, $y(2)=\dfrac{\pi^2-8}{4}$, then $y^2(0)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $u=\sin^{-1}\dfrac x2$, so $\dfrac{du}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}$ and the equation becomes $\dfrac{dy}{du}+uy=u^3$.
Integrating factor $e^{u^2/2}$: $ye^{u^2/2}=\displaystyle\int u^3e^{u^2/2}du=(u^2-2)e^{u^2/2}+c$.
$y=u^2-2+ce^{-u^2/2}$. At $x=2$, $u=\dfrac\pi2$: $\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}-2+ce^{-\pi^2/8}=\dfrac{\pi^2-8}{4}$, so $c=0$.
$y(0)=-2$, $y^2(0)=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: A bar magnet has total length $2l=20$ units and the field point P is at a distance $d=10$ units from the centre of the magnet. If the relative uncertainty of length measurement is 1%, then uncertainty of the magnetic field at point P is :
questions.note: NTA's final key gives 4% (option ID 6564452384) for all media, and also accepts 3% (option ID 6564452382) for the Hindi and Gujarati papers only, probably because of a translation issue there. The answer shown is the one for the English paper.
questions.sol:
P is on the perpendicular bisector of the magnet: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{m(2l)}{(d^2+l^2)^{3/2}}$.
Each length ($l$ and $d$) has a relative uncertainty of 1%, so
$\dfrac{\Delta B}{B}=\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}+\dfrac32\cdot\dfrac{2l^2\frac{\Delta l}{l}+2d^2\frac{\Delta d}{d}}{d^2+l^2}=1\%+3\%=4\%$.

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A)Angular Impulse(I)$[\mathrm{M^0L^2T^{-2}}]$
(B)Latent Heat(II)$[\mathrm{ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}}]$
(C)Electrical resistivity(III)$[\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}]$
(D)Electromotive force(IV)$[\mathrm{ML^3T^{-3}A^{-2}}]$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Angular impulse = change in angular momentum: $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}$ (III).
Latent heat = energy per unit mass: $\mathrm{L^2T^{-2}}$ (I).
Resistivity $\rho=RA/l$: $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}}\times\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{ML^3T^{-3}A^{-2}}$ (IV).
EMF = work per unit charge: $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}}$ (II).

questions.text: The velocity-time graph of an object moving along a straight line is shown in figure. What is the distance covered by the object between $t=0$ to $t=4$ s ?
questions.sol:
Distance = area under the $v$-$t$ graph from 0 to 4 s.
0 to 2 s: triangle, $\dfrac12\times2\times10=10$ m. 2 to 4 s: rectangle, $2\times10=20$ m.
Total $=30$ m.

questions.text: Earth has mass 8 times and radius 2 times that of a planet. If the escape velocity from the earth is 11.2 km/s, the escape velocity in km/s from the planet will be :
questions.sol:
$v_e=\sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}\propto\sqrt{\dfrac MR}$.
$\dfrac{v_{\text{earth}}}{v_{\text{planet}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{2}}=2$, so $v_{\text{planet}}=5.6$ km/s.

questions.text: A uniform rod of mass 250 g having length 100 cm is balanced on a sharp edge at 40 cm mark. A mass of 400 g is suspended at 10 cm mark. To maintain the balance of the rod, the mass to be suspended at 90 cm mark, is
questions.sol:
Take moments about the 40 cm mark.
Anticlockwise: $400\times30=12000$ g cm.
Clockwise: rod's weight at 50 cm gives $250\times10=2500$; the unknown mass gives $m\times50$.
$2500+50m=12000 \Rightarrow m=190$ g.

questions.text: A body of mass 4 kg is placed on a plane at a point P having coordinate (3, 4) m. Under the action of force $\vec{F}=\left(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}\right)$N, it moves to a new point Q having coordinates (6, 10)m in 4 sec. The average power and instantaneous power at the end of 4 sec are in the ratio of :
questions.sol:
Work $=\vec F\cdot\vec s=(2,3)\cdot(3,6)=24$ J, so average power $=24/4=6$ W.
Starting from rest, $\vec a=\vec F/m=(0.5,\,0.75)$ m s$^{-2}$ and $\vec v(4)=(2,3)$ m s$^{-1}$.
Instantaneous power $=\vec F\cdot\vec v=4+9=13$ W. Ratio $=6:13$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A balloon and its content having mass M is moving up with an acceleration 'a'. The mass that must be released from the content so that the balloon starts moving up with an acceleration '3a' will be
(Take 'g' as acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
Upthrust $U$ stays the same. Initially $U-Mg=Ma$, so $U=M(g+a)$.
After releasing $m$: $U-(M-m)g=(M-m)3a$, so $M-m=\dfrac{M(g+a)}{g+3a}$.
$m=M-\dfrac{M(g+a)}{g+3a}=\dfrac{2Ma}{3a+g}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A 400 g solid cube having an edge of length 10 cm floats in water. How much volume of the cube is outside the water ?
(Given : density of water $=1000$ kg m$^{-3}$)
questions.sol:
Floating: weight of water displaced = weight of cube = 400 g, so the submerged volume is 400 cm$^3$.
Cube volume $=1000$ cm$^3$, so $1000-400=600$ cm$^3$ is outside the water.

questions.text: The kinetic energy of translation of the molecules in 50 g of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas at $17^\circ$C is
questions.sol:
Translational KE $=\dfrac32nRT$ with $n=\dfrac{50}{44}$ mol and $T=290$ K.
$\dfrac32\times\dfrac{50}{44}\times8.3\times290\approx4102.8$ J (with $R=8.314$ it is about 4110 J; 4102.8 J is the closest option).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The ratio of vapour densities of two gases at the same temperature is $\dfrac{4}{25}$, then the ratio of r.m.s. velocities will be :
questions.sol:
Vapour density is proportional to molar mass, and $v_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt M}$.
$\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4}}=\dfrac52$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Knowing initial position $x_0$ and initial momentum $p_0$ is enough to determine the position and momentum at any time t for a simple harmonic motion with a given angular frequency $\omega$.
Reason (R) : The amplitude and phase can be expressed in terms of $x_0$ and $p_0$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
$x=A\sin(\omega t+\phi)$ with $x_0=A\sin\phi$ and $p_0=m\omega A\cos\phi$.
So $A=\sqrt{x_0^2+\left(\dfrac{p_0}{m\omega}\right)^2}$ and $\tan\phi=\dfrac{m\omega x_0}{p_0}$: amplitude and phase follow from $x_0,p_0$ (R true).
With $A$, $\phi$ and $\omega$ known, $x(t)$ and $p(t)$ are fixed for all $t$ (A true), and R is the reason.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 1 $\mu$F is charged to a potential difference of 20 V. The distance between plates is 1 $\mu$m. The energy density between plates of capacitor is.
questions.sol:
$E=\dfrac Vd=\dfrac{20}{10^{-6}}=2\times10^7$ V/m.
$u=\dfrac12\varepsilon_0E^2=\dfrac12\times8.85\times10^{-12}\times4\times10^{14}\approx1.8\times10^3$ J/m$^3$.

questions.text: An infinite wire has a circular bend of radius a, and carrying a current I as shown in figure. The magnitude of magnetic field at the origin O of the arc is given by :
questions.sol:
Upper straight part: its line passes through O, so it gives no field.
Lower straight part: semi-infinite, starting at the foot of the perpendicular from O at distance $a$: $\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi a}$.
Three-quarter circular arc: $\dfrac34\cdot\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2a}=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi a}\cdot\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.
Both are in the same direction (into the page), so $B=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac Ia\left[\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+1\right]$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T acts perpendicular to a circular copper disc 20 cm in radius. The disc is having a uniform angular velocity of $10\pi$ rad s$^{-1}$ about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to the disc. What is the potential difference developed between the axis of the disc and the rim ? ($\pi=3.14$)
questions.sol:
For a rotating disc, $\varepsilon=\dfrac12B\omega r^2$.
$\varepsilon=\dfrac12\times0.4\times10\pi\times(0.2)^2=0.08\pi=0.2512$ V.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The magnetic field of an E.M. wave is given by $\vec{B}=\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\hat{i}+\dfrac{1}{2}\hat{j}\right)30\sin\left[\omega\left(t-\dfrac{z}{c}\right)\right]$ (S.I. Units).
The corresponding electric field in S.I. units is :
questions.sol:
The disturbance travels along $+z$, in phase with $\vec B$, and $|E|=c|B|$.
$\vec E\times\vec B$ must point along $+\hat k$, which gives $\vec E=c\,\vec B\times\hat k$.
$\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\hat i+\dfrac12\hat j\right)\times\hat k=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\hat j+\dfrac12\hat i$.
So $\vec E=\left(\dfrac12\hat i-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\hat j\right)30c\sin\left[\omega\left(t-\dfrac zc\right)\right]$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a long glass tube, mixture of two liquids A and B with refractive indices 1.3 and 1.4 respectively, forms a convex refractive meniscus towards A. If an object placed at 13 cm from the vertex of the meniscus in A forms an image with a magnification of '$-2$' then the radius of curvature of meniscus is :
questions.sol:
Light goes from A ($n_1=1.3$) into B ($n_2=1.4$); $u=-13$ cm.
$m=\dfrac{n_1v}{n_2u}=-2 \Rightarrow v=\dfrac{-2\times1.4\times(-13)}{1.3}=28$ cm.
$\dfrac{n_2}{v}-\dfrac{n_1}{u}=\dfrac{n_2-n_1}{R}$: $\dfrac{1.4}{28}+\dfrac{1.3}{13}=0.15=\dfrac{0.1}{R}$, so $R=\dfrac23$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A concave mirror produces an image of an object such that the distance between the object and image is 20 cm. If the magnification of the image is '$-3$', then the magnitude of the radius of curvature of the mirror is :
questions.sol:
$m=-\dfrac vu=-3$, so $v=3u$ (real image, same side). The separation is $2|u|=20$ cm, so $u=-10$ cm, $v=-30$ cm.
$\dfrac1f=\dfrac1v+\dfrac1u=-\dfrac1{30}-\dfrac1{10}=-\dfrac{2}{15}$, $f=-7.5$ cm.
$|R|=2|f|=15$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The frequency of revolution of the electron in Bohr's orbit varies with n, the principal quantum number as
questions.sol:
In Bohr's model $v\propto\dfrac1n$ and $r\propto n^2$.
Frequency $f=\dfrac{v}{2\pi r}\propto\dfrac{1}{n^3}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of the following phenomena can not be explained by wave theory of light ?
questions.sol:
Reflection, refraction and diffraction are all explained by treating light as a spreading disturbance.
The Compton effect (the increase in $\lambda$ of X-rays scattered by electrons) needs photons carrying energy $h\nu$ and momentum $h/\lambda$, so it is the one that cannot be explained that way.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: In the circuit shown here, assuming threshold voltage of diode is negligibly small, then voltage $V_{AB}$ is correctly represented by :
options: $V_{AB}$ would be zero at all times
questions.sol:
The diode is in the lower lead, pointing from the source towards B, so current can only flow source $\to$ diode $\to$ B $\to$ R $\to$ A $\to$ source.
When it conducts, current flows through R from B to A, so B is at the higher potential and $V_{AB}$ is negative; in the other half-cycle no current flows and $V_{AB}=0$.
So $V_{AB}$ shows only negative half-cycles: graph (4).

questions.text:
The volume contraction of a solid copper cube of edge length 10 cm, when subjected to a hydraulic pressure of $7\times10^6$ Pa, would be __________ mm$^3$.
(Given bulk modulus of copper $=1.4\times10^{11}$ N m$^{-2}$)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electric dipole of dipole moment $6\times10^{-6}$ Cm is placed in uniform electric field of magnitude $10^6$ V/m. Initially, the dipole moment is parallel to electric field. The work that needs to be done on the dipole to make its dipole moment opposite to the field, will be __________ J.
questions.sol:
$W=pE(\cos0^\circ-\cos180^\circ)=2pE$.
$W=2\times6\times10^{-6}\times10^6=12$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The value of current I in the electrical circuit as given below, when potential at A is equal to the potential at B, will be __________ A.
questions.sol:
$V_A=V_B$ means the bridge is balanced: $\dfrac{10}{20}=\dfrac{R}{40}$, so $R=20\ \Omega$ and no current flows in the 30 $\Omega$ resistor.
Upper branch $10+20=30\ \Omega$, lower branch $20+40=60\ \Omega$; in parallel, $20\ \Omega$.
$I=\dfrac{40}{20}=2$ A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A conducting bar moves on two conducting rails as shown in the figure. A constant magnetic field B exists into the page. The bar starts to move from the vertex at time $t=0$ with a constant velocity. If the induced EMF is $E\propto t^n$, then value of n is __________.
questions.sol:
The rails form a V with its vertex at the start. At time $t$ the bar has moved $vt$, so the length of bar between the rails is proportional to $t$.
$E=Blv\propto t$, so $n=1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin transparent film with refractive index 1.4, is held on circular ring of radius 1.8 cm. The fluid in the film evaporates such that transmission through the film at wavelength 560 nm goes to a minimum every 12 seconds. Assuming that the film is flat on its two sides, the rate of evaporation is __________ $\pi\times10^{-13}$ m$^3$/s.
questions.sol:
Successive transmission minima correspond to a change of $\lambda$ in the path difference $2\mu t$, i.e. a change in thickness of $\dfrac{\lambda}{2\mu}=\dfrac{560}{2.8}=200$ nm.
Volume lost every 12 s $=\pi r^2\times200\times10^{-9}=\pi\times3.24\times10^{-4}\times2\times10^{-7}=6.48\pi\times10^{-11}$ m$^3$.
Rate $=\dfrac{6.48\pi\times10^{-11}}{12}=54\pi\times10^{-13}$ m$^3$/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are not correct with respect to energy of atomic orbitals of hydrogen atom ?
(A) 1s < 2p < 3d < 4s
(B) 1s < 2s = 2p < 3s = 3p
(C) 1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p
(D) 1s < 2s < 4s < 3d
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
In the hydrogen atom the orbital energy depends only on $n$.
(A) $n$ increases along the list: correct. (B) equal $n$ shown as equal: correct.
(C) puts $2s<2p$ and $3s<3p$: not correct. (D) puts $4s<3d$: not correct.
So (C) and (D) are not correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic transformation starting from the point A and coming back to the same point by tracing the path A$\to$B$\to$C$\to$D$\to$A as shown in the three cases above.
Choose the correct option regarding $\Delta U$ :
questions.sol:
Internal energy is a state function. In every case the gas returns to A, so $\Delta U=0$ for each cycle.
Hence $\Delta U$ is the same (zero) in all three cases.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Assume a living cell with 0.9%($\omega/\omega$) of glucose solution (aqueous). This cell is immersed in another solution having equal mole fraction of glucose and water.
(Consider the data upto first decimal place only)
The cell will :
options: show no change in volume since solution is 0.9%($\omega/\omega$)
shrink since solution is 0.45%($\omega/\omega$) as a result of association of glucose molecules (due to hydrogen bonding)
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. Equal mole fractions of glucose and water correspond to about 90.9% glucose by mass, which does not match any option. The answer index here is only a placeholder.
questions.sol:
Equal mole fractions mean 1 mol glucose (180 g) per mol water (18 g): glucose is $\dfrac{180}{198}\approx90.9\%$ by mass.
Such an outside solution is far more concentrated than the 0.9% cell fluid, so water would leave the cell and it would shrink; but none of the percentages in the options matches the data.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Concentrated nitric acid is labelled as 75% by mass. The volume in mL of the solution which contains 30 g of nitric acid is __________.
Given : Density of nitric acid solution is 1.25 g/mL.
questions.sol:
Mass of solution containing 30 g acid $=\dfrac{30}{0.75}=40$ g.
Volume $=\dfrac{40}{1.25}=32$ mL.

questions.text:
Arrange the following in increasing order of solubility product :
$\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$, AgBr, PbS, HgS
questions.sol:
Approximate $K_{sp}$ values: HgS $\sim10^{-52}$, PbS $\sim10^{-28}$, AgBr $\sim5\times10^{-13}$, $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ $\sim5\times10^{-6}$.
Increasing order: HgS < PbS < AgBr < $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For bacterial growth in a cell culture, growth law is very similar to the law of radioactive decay. Which of the following graphs is most suitable to represent bacterial colony growth ?
Where N - Number of Bacteria at any time, $N_0$ - Initial number of Bacteria.
questions.sol:
Growth follows a first-order law like decay but with a positive rate: $\dfrac{dN}{dt}=kN$, so $\dfrac{N}{N_0}=e^{kt}$.
The graph starts at $\dfrac{N}{N_0}=1$ at $t=0$ and rises ever more steeply: graph (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider an elementary reaction
$\mathrm{A(g)+B(g)\to C(g)+D(g)}$
If the volume of reaction mixture is suddenly reduced to $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of its initial volume, the reaction rate will become '$x$' times of the original reaction rate. The value of $x$ is :
questions.sol:
For the elementary reaction, rate $=k[\mathrm A][\mathrm B]$.
Reducing the volume to one third triples each concentration, so the rate becomes $3\times3=9$ times.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the inorganic sulphides that are yellow in colour :
(A) $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2S}$
(B) PbS
(C) CuS
(D) $\mathrm{As_2S_3}$
(E) $\mathrm{As_2S_5}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.note: I first took only (D) and (E) as yellow, since pure ammonium sulphide is colourless. The final key gives (A), (D) and (E), counting the yellow colour of ammonium sulphide solution; the answer here follows the final key.
questions.sol:
PbS and CuS are black precipitates.
$\mathrm{As_2S_3}$ and $\mathrm{As_2S_5}$ are yellow.
Ammonium sulphide solution is yellow (it usually contains polysulphide), and the final key counts it as yellow too.
So (A), (D) and (E).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : According to the Law of Octaves, the elements were arranged in the increasing order of their atomic number.
Statement (II) : Meyer observed a periodically repeated pattern upon plotting physical properties of certain elements against their respective atomic numbers.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Newlands arranged elements in increasing order of atomic weight (Law of Octaves): Statement I is false.
Lothar Meyer plotted physical properties (atomic volume, melting point, boiling point) against atomic weight: Statement II is false.
Both are false.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: The amphoteric oxide among $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{V_2O_4}$ and $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$, upon reaction with alkali leads to formation of an oxide anion. The oxidation state of V in the oxide anion is :
questions.sol:
Basic character falls as the oxidation state rises: $\mathrm{V_2O_3}$ basic, $\mathrm{V_2O_4}$ less basic, $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ amphoteric.
$\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ reacts with alkali to give vanadate, $\mathrm{VO_4^{3-}}$, in which V is $+5$.

Given below are two statements :
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.text:
Identify product [A], [B] and [C] in the following reaction sequence.
$\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH\xrightarrow[H_2]{Pd/C}[A]\xrightarrow[(ii)\ Zn,\ H_2O]{(i)\ O_3}[B]+[C]}$
questions.sol:
Partial hydrogenation of propyne stops at the alkene: [A] is propene, $\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2}$.
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C: $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ ([B]) and HCHO ([C]).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is :
questions.sol:
The substrate is $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Ph)-CHBr-CH_2-CHBr-CH_2CH_3}$ (3,5-dibromo-2-phenylheptane).
Excess alcoholic KOH removes both HBr by E2. Loss of the benzylic H gives C2=C3, conjugated with the ring; loss of H from C4 gives C4=C5, conjugated with C2=C3.
Product: $\mathrm{CH_3-C(Ph)=CH-CH=CH-CH_2CH_3}$, 2-phenylhepta-2,4-diene.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The product B formed in the following reaction sequence is :
questions.note: Options (2) and (4) show the same structure as printed.
questions.sol:
HCl adds to the side-chain C=C through the more stable benzylic carbocation, so A is $\mathrm{Ar-CHCl-CH_2CH_3}$ (Ar = 4-methylphenyl).
AgCN is mainly covalent and attacks through nitrogen, giving the isocyanide: B is $\mathrm{Ar-CH(NC)-CH_2CH_3}$, structure (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The total number of compounds from below when treated with hot $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ giving benzoic acid is :
questions.sol:
Hot $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ oxidises a side chain to $-\mathrm{COOH}$ only if the carbon attached to the ring carries at least one H.
Toluene, ethylbenzene, cumene, isobutylbenzene and propylbenzene: yes (5).
tert-Butylbenzene and 2-phenylpropan-2-ol: no benzylic H. 4,4'-Dimethylbiphenyl gives a biphenyl dicarboxylic acid, not benzoic acid.
Total $=5$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify correct statements :
(A) Primary amines do not give diazonium salts when treated with $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ in acidic condition.
(B) Aliphatic and aromatic primary amines on heating with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and ethanolic KOH form carbylamines.
(C) Secondary and tertiary amines also give carbylamine test.
(D) Benzenesulfonyl chloride is known as Hinsberg's reagent.
(E) Tertiary amines reacts with benzenesulfonyl chloride very easily.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) False: primary amines do give diazonium salts with $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$/acid (aryl ones are stable at 273-278 K).
(B) True: carbylamine reaction of primary amines.
(C) False: only primary amines give it.
(D) True.
(E) False: tertiary amines have no N-H and do not react with it.
So (B) and (D).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
(Saccharides)		List - II
(Glycosidic-linkages found)
(A)Sucrose(I)$\alpha\,1-4$
(B)Maltose(II)$\alpha\,1-4$ and $\alpha\,1-6$
(C)Lactose(III)$\alpha\,1-\beta\,2$
(D)Amylopectin(IV)$\beta\,1-4$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Sucrose: C1 of $\alpha$-glucose to C2 of $\beta$-fructose, $\alpha1-\beta2$ (III).
Maltose: $\alpha1-4$ (I).
Lactose: $\beta$-galactose C1 to glucose C4, $\beta1-4$ (IV).
Amylopectin: $\alpha1-4$ chains with $\alpha1-6$ branches (II).

questions.text:
Identify correct conversion during acidic hydrolysis from the following :
(A) starch gives galactose.
(B) cane sugar gives equal amount of glucose and fructose.
(C) milk sugar gives glucose and galactose.
(D) amylopectin gives glucose and fructose.
(E) amylose gives only glucose.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Starch, amylose and amylopectin are polymers of $\alpha$-D-glucose and give only glucose: (A) and (D) are wrong, (E) is right.
Cane sugar (sucrose) gives equimolar glucose and fructose: (B) right.
Milk sugar (lactose) gives glucose and galactose: (C) right.
So (B), (C) and (E).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following data :
Heat of formation of $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}=-393.5$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
Heat of formation of $\mathrm{H_2O(l)}=-286.0$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
Heat of combustion of benzene $=-3267.0$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
The heat of formation of benzene is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
(Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_6(l)}+\dfrac{15}{2}\mathrm{O_2}\to6\mathrm{CO_2}+3\mathrm{H_2O}$.
$\Delta_cH=6(-393.5)+3(-286.0)-\Delta_fH(\mathrm{C_6H_6})=-3219-\Delta_fH$.
$-3267=-3219-\Delta_fH \Rightarrow \Delta_fH=+48$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Electrolysis of 600 mL aqueous solution of NaCl for 5 min changes the pH of the solution to 12. The current in Amperes used for the given electrolysis is __________. (Nearest integer).
questions.sol:
pH 12 means $[\mathrm{OH^-}]=10^{-2}$ M, so $0.6\times10^{-2}=6\times10^{-3}$ mol of $\mathrm{OH^-}$ formed, needing $6\times10^{-3}$ mol of electrons.
Charge $=6\times10^{-3}\times96500=579$ C.
$I=\dfrac{579}{300}\approx1.93\approx2$ A.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Total number of molecules/species from following which will be paramagnetic is __________.
$\mathrm{O_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2^+}$, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$, NO, $\mathrm{NO_2}$, CO, $\mathrm{K_2[NiCl_4]}$, $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}$, $\mathrm{K_2[Ni(CN)_4]}$
questions.sol:
Paramagnetic: $\mathrm{O_2}$ (2 unpaired), $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ and $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ (1 each), NO and $\mathrm{NO_2}$ (odd electron), $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ (tetrahedral $d^8$, 2 unpaired).
Diamagnetic: CO, $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ (low spin $d^6$), $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ (square planar $d^8$).
Total $=6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A group 15 element forms $d\pi-d\pi$ bond with transition metals. It also forms hydride, which is a strongest base among the hydrides of other group members that form $d\pi-d\pi$ bond. The atomic number of the element is __________.
questions.sol:
Nitrogen has no d orbitals, so the elements that form $d\pi-d\pi$ bonds are P, As, Sb and Bi.
Basic strength of the hydrides falls down the group ($\mathrm{PH_3}>\mathrm{AsH_3}>\mathrm{SbH_3}>\mathrm{BiH_3}$), so the element is phosphorus.
Atomic number $=15$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The spin only magnetic moment ($\mu$) value (B.M.) of the compound with strongest oxidising power among $\mathrm{Mn_2O_3}$, TiO and VO is __________ B.M. (Nearest integer).
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ ($d^4$) is strongly oxidising because it gains an electron to reach stable $d^5$ $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$; $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$ are reducing.
$\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ in $\mathrm{Mn_2O_3}$ (high spin $d^4$) has 4 unpaired electrons: $\mu=\sqrt{4\times6}=\sqrt{24}\approx4.9\approx5$ B.M.
questions.subject: Chemistry
